fixes.explanation: Abraham is a big name in the Bible, so I see the thinking, friend. But the psalm gives the credit somewhere else. It says, "Know that the LORD is God. It is He who made us…" (Psalm 100:3). The LORD made us.
Moses is a big name, friend, but he isn't named anywhere in this psalm. The psalm says, "Know that the LORD is God. It is He who made us…" (Psalm 100:3). The LORD is the one who made us.
The psalm says the opposite, friend. Right after saying who made us, it says, "…and we are His; we are His people…" (Psalm 100:3). It says it twice, back to back.
Right on, baker. The psalm says, "Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise…" (Psalm 100:4). That's what you carry through the gate, a grateful heart and a song.

True, friend. The verse ends, "give thanks to Him and bless His name." (Psalm 100:4). Thanks and blessing go together at the close of that verse. So the psalm does tell people to bless the LORD's name.

An enemy running off is a fair guess, friend, but this psalm doesn't mention one. The reason it gives is, "For the LORD is good, and His loving devotion endures forever…" (Psalm 100:5). His goodness is the reason.
